note: Re-judged 2026-10-11 by an independent judge after the fix round (2691e815b1). RFC 4555 4.2.6: "The Notify Message Type for this message is 16402.  The notification data contains the IP addresses and ports from/to which the packet was sent." Type clause, now enforced: TestMobikeNoNATsDataIsTheSendTuple decrypts the NO_NATS_ALLOWED notify off a real update and requires NotifyMsgType == 16402 as a literal, so a wrong shared wire.NotifyNoNATsAllowed constant is red (mbRequireNotify finds the notify by the constant, then the literal disagrees) and a producer writing another type is red at mbRequireNotify. Data clause: the 12-octet IPv4 data equals the received packet's source address, destination address, source port and destination port field by field, and noNATsAllowedMatches accepts that tuple. Negative: noNATsAllowedMatches refuses a changed source address, a changed destination address, swapped ports, a changed source port, and now the packet's own addresses and ports written at the 16-octet width; because net.IP.Equal treats the IPv4-mapped form as equal, the length test is the only thing that refuses that last case, so it isolates the width. Revert records on mobike.go::noNATsAllowedPayload (positive) and noNATsAllowedMatches (negative). Both defects of the earlier weak verdict are resolved.
